#+title: Working with immutable build products

* A normal edit
Keep the compiler VM warm for source analysis and ordinary evaluation. Native
preparation happens when a product is needed. Application-only edits reuse the
native product; Rust and toolchain changes create a new one. The selected
library and each preparation's receipt make that distinction visible.

* Two people or two agent sessions
Each request has its own retained result. Identical Nix derivations can share
production without sharing a writable Cargo target. Session state and product
identity stay separate. A disconnected requester does not establish that a
shared daemon build was cancelled. Per-subscriber cancellation and durable job
reconnection need an explicit coordinator policy.

* A failed build
The error belongs to preparation. The old native selection stays usable.
Inspect the failed command's bounded log and compare the new source snapshot
with the working receipt. Keep an artifact capsule when reporting a successful
product whose runtime behavior fails a later test.

* A runtime update
Prepare the candidate first. Compare its identity, run the intended consumer
checks, then start a compatible fresh VM or use the runtime's supported code
activation protocol. Native libraries, in-VM generation ownership, serving
readiness and application-data migration are separate decisions.

* Capabilities and their delivery state
| Capability | Available surface | Scope |
| Immutable native preparation | artifacts prepare; artifact/prepare-native! | Standalone locked Linux x86_64 cdylib crates; workspace/path dependencies remain unsupported |
| Application production | bl build; build/run; artifact/prepare-application! | Exact SDK, declared roots, remote Nix production, verified units and claimed publication; ordinary managed CLI control passes |
| Scoped application composition | build/run with :scope :scoped | Verified immutable parent, existing compiler ownership rules, retained units and complete new product; worker/receiver/frontend controls pass; combined SDK gate remains |
| Compiler generations | Nix compiler product | Existing independent A/B/C producer and fresh boots; B/C bytes agree |
| SDK and release products | Nix SDK and portable outputs | Automatic immutable SDK selection; Source-free loading and corruption/missing-unit refusals pass; complete promotion remains pending |
| Release publication | bl self-build --out BIN | Verified Nix release bytes under destination custody; ordinary publication and isolated no-Nix native JSON receiver pass |
| Ordinary build integration | Normal checkout/build commands | Nix-only Source/runtime refresh and pinned prerequisites before BEAM |
| Authenticated command executor | Managed platform and automatic checkout staging | Exact helper digest/protocol checked before commands; no ambient Rust required |
| Managed build-host policy | nixosModules.artifacts | Strict sandbox and aggregate worker limits; apply and validate through host deployment |
| Explicit retention | Per-request Nix roots and receipts | Conservative retention; automatic live-consumer GC remains a separate gate |
| Product inspection | artifacts list | Stored successful receipts |
| Candidate comparison | artifacts compare | Identity changes; compatibility needs runtime checks |
| Reproduction descriptors | artifacts capsule | Verified artifact/source and runtime identities; test qualification stays explicit |
| Executable NIF showcase | examples/artifacts/showcase.bl | Real Rustler preparation and invocation |
| Environment preparation | Pinned recipe and platform lock | Rust/compiler/vendor closure; broader native system-dependency recipes need declared support |
| Shared production | Nix derivation identity | Independent clients/roots; durable subscription UI is coordinator work |
| Remote reuse | Existing Nix daemon configuration | Remote worker/target/cache trust requires environment qualification |
| Comparison realms | Exact product addresses are available | Realm orchestration and state isolation remain runtime integration work |
| Failure capsules with test replay | Artifact descriptor exists | Test selection/receipt attachment and replay UI remain integration work |
| Source-to-artifact impact explanations | Native comparison and application result graph | Application result records content/interface/closure keys and requirements; joined explanation UI remains pending |
| Bounded production workers | Fixed-memory KVM guests and disk-backed scratch | Native/SDK workers are bounded; aggregate admission and cost-aware scheduling need their coordinator gates |
| Rollback | Prior artifacts remain retained | Activation, compatibility and data restore use the existing Foundry/runtime contracts |

* Boundaries that stay with the language
Compiler semantics, hygienic expansion, descriptor truth, execution admission,
actor/callback lifetimes and retirement of running code belong to Beam Lisp.
Nix supplies filesystem products. Foundry coordinates preparation and deployment.
Actual runtime loading and qualification determine what those products can do.

* Declared application inputs
Keep namespace roots in :paths and :build :paths. Declare supporting files or
directories outside those roots with :build :inputs. For example:

#+begin_src clojure
{:paths ["src"]
 :build {:paths ["src"] :inputs ["schemas" "assets"] :out "build" :jobs 2}}
#+end_src

The snapshot includes file bytes, executable bits, empty directories and declared
supporting files. Generated state and the selected output are excluded. Selected
symlinks and inputs outside the project root are refused. A failed preparation
leaves the selected product intact. Application worker parallelism is bounded
by its four CPUs even when a declaration requests a larger maximum.

The output's .nix-product names its immutable generation; units/ contains its
verified namespace units. A declared :build :world selects contextual production.
Its artifact-unit/ is a link to the complete immutable paired unit, preserving
the verifier's physical directory identity. Individual member links cannot
substitute for that boundary. Compatibility beam links and build diagnostics are
projections. Engine-checkout builds instead select the SDK through image/, lib/
and .nix-sdk. These filesystem selections do not activate code or confer SDK
authority. Runtime activation still uses the language's verified-unit protocol.

Compiler controls call build/produce! explicitly. Its internal bootstrap entry
is copied into the Nix producer tree; normal checkout commands clear that mode.
Project :env values remain command data and do not choose the startup SDK or
artifact platform. Existing bounded-constructor restrictions still apply to
artifact production, including the recorded environment-reading macro refusal.

* Checking an already produced SDK
The production receiver control does not rerun the compiler or synthesize SDK
inventory entries. Supply the selected SDK, its pinned Elixir executable and
an absent evidence directory:

#+begin_src sh
systemd-run --user --collect --wait --pipe \
  --working-directory="$PWD" --property=MemoryMax=2G --property=MemorySwapMax=0 \
  scripts/check-produced-sdk --sdk /nix/store/SELECTED-SDK \
    --elixir /nix/store/PINNED-ELIXIR/bin/elixir --out .local/sdk-receiver
#+end_src

It copies the actual image, removes language Source, and uses fresh VMs for
positive loading, corrupt-byte refusal and missing-inventory-row refusal. Logs
and exact input identities remain in the evidence directory. The control does
not certify the complete contextual matrix, all native libraries or deployment
promotion. The portable-runtime Nix control separately runs the release in an
FHS receiver with /nix/store absent and calls the JSON NIF directly.

* Partial source ownership
Ordinary CLI builds keep their complete-inventory meaning. Existing programmatic
callers that supply a subset retain the :scope :scoped contract:

#+begin_src clojure
(build/run {:root project-root :out build-directory
            :sources [(str project-root "/src/example/leaf.bl")]
            :scope :scoped :jobs 2})
#+end_src

Nix verifies and consumes the selected parent product. The existing compiler
updates that private generation; unrelated source facts, modules and artifact
units remain retained. Publication selects a complete immutable result under
the existing writer claim. An empty scope retains the generation's contents.
A subsequent full inventory prunes removed sources. Unknown scopes and failed
compilation leave the selected generation intact. A changed SDK requires a
full build, and contextual World products use full ownership.
